gmaps.OfWhatItWouldCost: of what it would have cost
gmaps.EstimateWarningTitle: The cost figures are an estimate, not the invoice.
gmaps.EstimateWarningBody: Google's price bands are monthly and project-wide: a period that is not a calendar month prices a volume Google never saw, and another application sharing the key eats the same free allowance. The map, the autocomplete and the pin-drag geocoder are also counted from what the application reports rather than measured by the server.
gmaps.DailyChartTitle: Requests per day: bought vs cached
gmaps.DailyChartHint: The red band is what you pay. Red shrinking while green grows is exactly what a cache is for.
gmaps.TrendHint: This line should climb and then level off: those are the origin-destination pairs that repeat week after week.
gmaps.BySkuHint: Free remaining is for the current calendar month, not the selected period: it is the figure you set Cloud Console quotas against. Reported marks the products counted by the application rather than the server.
gmaps.TrafficModeHint: MaxSavings asks for routes without traffic ($5 per 1,000, 10,000 free a month) and adds our own margin. Precision asks for Google's predicted traffic for the trip's hour.
gmaps.PrecisionWarningBody: $10 per 1,000 requests instead of $5, and the free allowance drops from 10,000 to 5,000 a month. The cache still works the same, but every request it misses is billed at double.
gmaps.CacheHint: Retention decides how long a Google answer is served and kept, from 1 to 3,650 days. Google's terms describe a 30-day window for cached content; the default of 365 is a deliberate business decision, not an oversight. The margin is the percentage added to the free-flow time in MaxSavings mode.
gmaps.SaveHint: Changes take effect system-wide within a minute, with no release.
gmaps.Saved: Saved. Live system-wide within a minute.

gmaps.PricingHint: These prices live in the database rather than in code: when Google changes them, they are corrected without shipping a version.
gmaps.PricingPer1000: All per 1,000 requests. Bands are monthly and per SKU.

import.problem.DUPLICATE_ACTIVE_TRIP.fix: The same patient already has this ride on this date, between the same two addresses, in the same window. If this row IS that trip, put its TripId on the row so it updates the existing one instead of duplicating it. If it is a different journey, change the day, the window or one of the addresses. If it is neither, leave it out of the file.
import.problem.TRIP_CANCELLED.title: The trip exists, but it is cancelled
import.problem.TRIP_CANCELLED.fix: A cancelled trip is not brought back by importing it again — that would put a vehicle on a route for a journey the office had closed. Uncancel it from the trips list, or book it as a new trip with a TripId of its own.
The patient cannot be told apart

With no rider ID, the patient is matched on name plus phone. A name on its own would merge two people who happen to share one, and each would see the other's trips. Add the rider ID, or the phone number.
import.problem.INVALID_TRIP_ID.title: The row has no TripId
import.problem.INVALID_TRIP_ID.fix: The TripId is what an import is matched on. Without it, a trip that already exists cannot be told apart from a new booking, so nothing can be stored. Take it from the broker's file.
import.problem.DUPLICATE_RIDER_ID.title: That rider ID belongs to another patient
import.problem.DUPLICATE_RIDER_ID.fix: Somebody else is already filed under this rider ID. It is nearly always a typo in the file. Correcting it here fixes this row; if the file has it wrong on every row, fix it there and import again.
import.problem.DUPLICATE_RECORD.title: Another uniqueness rule refused it
import.problem.DUPLICATE_RECORD.fix: Something in this row already exists and may only exist once, and it is not one of the cases this screen knows how to explain. Export the row and send it to support with the reference below.
import.problem.INVALID_REFERENCE.title: It points at something that is not there
import.problem.INVALID_REFERENCE.fix: The row names a payer, a space type or a patient that does not exist in the system. Check the payer chosen at the top of this screen first — that is the usual cause.
import.problem.MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD.ti: Something it cannot be stored without is empty
import.problem.MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD.fi: Fill in the fields below. A trip needs at least an identifier, a date, a patient and both addresses.
import.problem.FIELD_TOO_LONG.title: An address is longer than the column
import.problem.FIELD_TOO_LONG.fix: Addresses are stored up to 450 characters. Shorten it: dropping the country, or a floor and suite number that the comment already carries, is usually enough.
import.problem.CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT.titl: Something else was touching the same record
import.problem.CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT.fix: Nothing is wrong with this row. Send it again.
import.problem.TIMEOUT.title: The database did not answer in time
import.problem.TIMEOUT.fix: Nothing is wrong with this row. Send it again — and if it keeps happening, wait a couple of minutes first.
import.problem.INTERNAL_ERROR.title: The server could not say what went wrong
import.problem.INTERNAL_ERROR.fix: This one is ours, not the file's. The reference below is the key to the full record on the server — send it to support. Importing the file again is safe, and is sometimes enough.
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_TRIP_ID.title: The row has no TripId
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_TRIP_ID.fix: Caught before anything was sent. The TripId is what an import is matched on — without it a trip that already exists cannot be told from a new booking. Take it from the broker's file.
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_PATIENT_IDENTITY: The patient cannot be told apart
Caught before anything was sent. Add the rider ID or the phone number: with neither, two patients who share a name become one record, and each would see the other's trips.
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_DATE.title: The row has no usable date
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_DATE.fix: The date column is empty, or it is in a format this layout does not use. Set the day here, or fix the column in the file and import it again.
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_ADDRESS.title: One end of the journey is missing
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_ADDRESS.fix: A trip needs both a pickup and a dropoff address. Fill in the one that is empty.
import.problem.LOCAL_ADDRESS_TOO_LONG.ti: An address is longer than the column
import.problem.LOCAL_ADDRESS_TOO_LONG.fi: Caught before anything was sent. Addresses are stored up to 450 characters — dropping the country, or a floor and suite that the comment already carries, is usually enough.
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_COORDINATES.titl: The address could not be located
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_COORDINATES.fix: A warning, not a rejection — the trip was imported. But one end of the journey has no position, so it cannot be routed or shown on a map. Correct the address here, or find it later with the 'missing coordinates' filter on the trips list.
import.problem.LOCAL_MAPPING_FAILED.titl: The line could not be read as a trip
import.problem.LOCAL_MAPPING_FAILED.fix: The format of the file is wrong on this line — a shifted column, a stray quote, a merged cell. It has to be put right in the file itself; there is nothing here to edit.
import.problem.LOCAL_NOT_CONFIRMED.title: Sent, but the answer never arrived
import.problem.LOCAL_NOT_CONFIRMED.fix: It may or may not have gone in — the import stopped before the server answered. Send it again: trips are matched on the TripId, so if it did go in it is updated, never duplicated.
